technocrat.zh: 这位技术专家治国论者提出了一个新的经济计划。

technocrat.zh: 技术专家统治论者通常关注数据和效率。

expropriate.zh: 政府决定征用这块土地来修路。

expropriate.en: They tried to expropriate his property without compensation.
expropriate.zh: 他们试图在没有补偿的情况下没收他的财产。

brassy.zh: 她似黄铜般响亮的声音整个房间都能听到。

patrimony.zh: 他从祖父那里继承了一大笔祖传财物。

patrimony.zh: 教会的世袭财产包括许多历史建筑。

stylus.zh: 他用一支触控笔在平板上写字。

vibrancy.zh: 这座城市以其文化活力而闻名。

vibrancy.zh: 音乐的振响充满了音乐厅。

irreducible.zh: 这个问题不能简化成更简单的形式。

amulet.zh: 她带着护身符以求好运。

amulet.zh: 这个旧护身符能抵御邪灵。

germane.en: Please keep your questions germane to the topic.
germane.zh: 请让你的问题与主题相关。

discomfit.en: The unexpected question discomfited the speaker.
discomfit.zh: 这个意外的问题让演讲者感到挫败。

discomfit.en: She tried not to discomfit her guests with bad news.
discomfit.zh: 她尽量不用坏消息打乱客人的心情。

anodyne.en: The doctor prescribed an anodyne for the pain.
anodyne.zh: 医生开了止痛药来缓解疼痛。

anodyne.en: His anodyne comments did not help the situation.
anodyne.zh: 他止痛药般的评论没有帮助情况。

misinform.en: Do not misinform the public about the facts.
misinform.zh: 不要向公众提供错误的事实信息。

misinform.en: They tried to misinform us about the event.
misinform.zh: 他们试图就这个事件向我们提供错误消息。

fallibility.en: We must accept human fallibility in all decisions.
fallibility.zh: 我们必须接受人类在所有决策中的易错性。

fallibility.en: His fallibility became clear after the mistake.
fallibility.zh: 错误之后，他的易误性变得明显。

petulance.en: Her petulance annoyed everyone in the room.
petulance.zh: 她的坏脾气惹恼了房间里的每个人。

petulance.en: He spoke with petulance when he didn't get his way.
petulance.zh: 当他不顺心时，他说话带着易怒。

nonentity.en: The idea was dismissed as a complete nonentity.
nonentity.zh: 这个想法被认为完全不存在而被驳回。

nonentity.en: He felt like a nonentity in the large crowd.
nonentity.zh: 他在人群中感觉自己像个虚无。

deprecate.en: Many people deprecate the use of violence.
She deprecates his rude behavior in public.
deprecate.zh: 她反对他在公共场合的粗鲁行为。

comatose.en: The patient remained comatose after the accident.
comatose.zh: 事故后病人一直处于昏迷状态。

comatose.en: He was comatose from the medication for hours.
comatose.zh: 药物让他昏睡了几个小时。

cantankerous.en: The old man is known for his cantankerous nature.
cantankerous.zh: 这个老人以爱吵架的性格闻名。

cantankerous.en: She became cantankerous when she was tired.
cantankerous.zh: 她累的时候变得专爱唱反调。

unexceptional.en: The movie was unexceptional and quickly forgotten.
unexceptional.zh: 这部电影很平常，很快被遗忘。

unexceptional.en: His performance was unexceptional but acceptable.
unexceptional.zh: 他的表现不特别但可以接受。

sop.en: He gave a small sop to calm the angry customer.
sop.zh: 他给了点小贿赂来安抚生气的顾客。

sop.en: The sop of bread soaked up the soup.

ribald.en: His ribald jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
ribald.zh: 他下流的笑话让每个人都不舒服。

ribald.en: She avoided his ribald comments at the party.
ribald.zh: 她在派对上避开他粗俗的评论。

pugnacious.en: The pugnacious dog barked at every stranger.
pugnacious.zh: 好斗的狗对着每个陌生人吠叫。

pugnacious.en: He has a pugnacious attitude in debates.
pugnacious.zh: 他在辩论中有好斗的态度。

miff.en: She had a miff with her friend over a small thing.
miff.zh: 她因为一件小事和朋友发生了小争执。

miff.en: His rude comment caused a miff between them.
miff.zh: 他粗鲁的评论引起了他们之间的愠怒。

emasculate.en: The new law could emasculate the agency's power.
emasculate.zh: 新法律可能会削弱该机构的权力。

emasculate.en: He felt the criticism emasculated his authority.
emasculate.zh: 他觉得批评削弱了他的权威。

indolent.en: The indolent student never finished his homework.
indolent.zh: 懒惰的学生从不完成作业。

indolent.en: She was too indolent to get out of bed early.

emblematic.en: The dove is emblematic of peace and hope.
emblematic.zh: 鸽子是和平与希望的象征。

emblematic.en: His actions were emblematic of his true character.
emblematic.zh: 他的行为是他真实性格的典型体现。

crudity.en: The crudity of the painting surprised the critics.
crudity.zh: 这幅画的粗糙让评论家惊讶。

crudity.en: He was embarrassed by the crudity of his jokes.
crudity.zh: 他为自己笑话的粗俗感到尴尬。

pariah.en: After the scandal, he became a social pariah.
pariah.zh: 丑闻之后，他成了社会上的被放逐者。

pariah.en: She felt like a pariah in her own community.
pariah.zh: 她在自己的社区里感觉像个贱民。

salubrious.en: The mountain air is very salubrious for health.
salubrious.zh: 山里的空气对健康非常有益。

salubrious.en: They moved to a salubrious climate for their son.
salubrious.zh: 他们为了儿子搬到了有益健康的气候区。

garrulous.en: The garrulous old man talked for hours.
garrulous.zh: 饶舌的老人聊了几个小时。

garrulous.en: She is too garrulous to keep a secret.
garrulous.zh: 她太多嘴了，守不住秘密。

felicitous.en: Her felicitous choice of words impressed everyone.
felicitous.zh: 她巧妙的措辞给每个人留下了印象。

felicitous.en: The timing of his arrival was felicitous.
felicitous.zh: 他到达的时机极为适当。

bedlam.en: The classroom was complete bedlam after the bell.
bedlam.zh: 铃响后教室里一片混乱。

bedlam.en: The protest turned into bedlam very quickly.

villainous.en: The villainous character was hated by all.
villainous.zh: 罪恶的角色被所有人憎恨。

villainous.en: He played a villainous role in the movie.
villainous.zh: 他在电影中扮演了一个恶棍的角色。

sate.en: A big meal will sate your hunger for hours.
sate.zh: 一顿大餐会让你饱几个小时。

sate.en: He could not sate his thirst for knowledge.
sate.zh: 他无法满足对知识的渴望。

perspire.en: People perspire when they exercise heavily.
perspire.zh: 人们剧烈运动时会出汗。

perspire.en: She began to perspire in the hot sun.
perspire.zh: 她在炎热的太阳下开始流汗。

lackey.en: The rich man had a lackey to do his chores.
lackey.zh: 那个富人有个仆人做杂务。

lackey.en: He acted like a lackey to gain favor.
lackey.zh: 他表现得像个马屁精以获取好感。

invigorate.en: A cold shower can invigorate you in the morning.
invigorate.zh: 冷水澡能在早晨让你精力充沛。

invigorate.en: The fresh air invigorated the tired hikers.
invigorate.zh: 新鲜空气鼓舞了疲惫的徒步者。

indecipherable.zh: 他的笔迹完全辨读不出。

indecipherable.en: The code was indecipherable without the key.
indecipherable.zh: 没有密钥，密码无法破译。

dross.en: The gold was separated from the dross.
We must remove the dross from the metal.
dross.zh: 我们必须去除金属中的渣滓。

buxom.en: The buxom woman had a cheerful smile.
buxom.zh: 丰满的女人有着愉快的笑容。

buxom.en: She was described as buxom and healthy.
buxom.zh: 她被描述为健美而丰满。

acerbic.en: His acerbic wit often offended people.
acerbic.zh: 他尖刻的机智常常冒犯别人。

acerbic.en: The lemon had an acerbic taste.

ingratiating.en: She gave an ingratiating smile to the boss.
ingratiating.zh: 她对老板露出了逢迎的微笑。

ingratiating.en: His ingratiating manner made others suspicious.
ingratiating.zh: 他迎合的态度让别人起疑。

flaccid.en: The flaccid balloon lay on the floor.
flaccid.zh: 软塌塌的气球躺在地板上。

flaccid.en: His muscles became flaccid after the illness.
flaccid.zh: 生病后他的肌肉变得松弛无力。

composed.en: She remained composed during the crisis.
He was composed and ready to answer questions.
composed.zh: 他沉着冷静，准备好回答问题。

parsimony.en: His parsimony made him save every penny.
parsimony.zh: 他的吝啬让他省下每一分钱。

parsimony.en: The parsimony of the budget caused problems.
parsimony.zh: 预算的过度节俭导致了问题。

fulcrum.en: The seesaw needs a fulcrum to work.
fulcrum.zh: 跷跷板需要一个支点才能工作。

fulcrum.en: A lever rotates around its fulcrum.

sprain.en: She suffered a bad ankle sprain.
He tried to sprain his wrist playing tennis.
sprain.zh: 他打网球时试图扭伤手腕。

sneaking.en: He had a sneaking suspicion about her.
sneaking.zh: 他对她有一种暗中的怀疑。

sneaking.en: A sneaking feeling told him to leave.
sneaking.zh: 一种隐秘的感觉告诉他离开。

ostentation.en: His wealth was shown with great ostentation.
She disliked the ostentation of the party.

avaricious.en: The avaricious man wanted more money.
avaricious.zh: 那个贪婪的人想要更多钱。

avaricious.en: Her avaricious nature made her unpopular.
avaricious.zh: 她贪婪的本性让她不受欢迎。

outshine.en: Her talent will outshine everyone else.
outshine.zh: 她的才华将使其他人相形见绌。

outshine.en: He hopes to outshine his older brother.

miserly.en: The miserly man never shared his food.
miserly.zh: 那个吝啬的人从不分享食物。

miserly.en: Her miserly habits annoyed her friends.
miserly.zh: 她吝啬的习惯惹恼了朋友。

ingratiate.en: He tried to ingratiate himself with the boss.
She ingratiated herself by bringing gifts.
ingratiate.zh: 她通过带礼物来讨好别人。

desirous.en: She is desirous of a new job.
He felt desirous of her attention.

defray.en: The company will defray your travel costs.
defray.zh: 公司将支付你的旅行费用。

defray.en: He used savings to defray the expenses.

underling.en: The manager gave orders to his underling.
underling.zh: 经理给他的下属下命令。

underling.en: She treated every underling with respect.

superficiality.en: His superficiality was clear in his speech.
superficiality.zh: 他的肤浅在讲话中很明显。

superficiality.en: She criticized the superficiality of the report.

penury.en: They lived in penury after losing their jobs.
penury.zh: 失业后他们生活在贫困中。

penury.en: Penury forced him to beg on the streets.

infernal.en: The infernal noise kept me awake.
infernal.zh: 那恶魔般的噪音让我睡不着。

infernal.en: He spoke of infernal creatures in the story.
infernal.zh: 他故事里提到了阴间的生物。

impecunious.en: The impecunious student could not pay rent.
impecunious.zh: 那个身无分文的学生付不起房租。

impecunious.en: He remained impecunious despite working hard.
impecunious.zh: 尽管努力工作，他仍然贫穷。

histrionic.en: Her histrionic behavior annoyed the audience.
histrionic.zh: 她矫揉造作的行为惹恼了观众。

histrionic.en: He gave a histrionic performance on stage.
histrionic.zh: 他在舞台上进行了戏剧性的表演。

dissemble.en: He tried to dissemble his true feelings.
She dissembled her anger with a smile.

vexation.en: The delay caused him great vexation.
Her vexation was clear from her frown.
vexation.zh: 她的烦恼从皱眉中可见。

tempestuous.zh: 他们暴风雨般的关系很快结束了。

tempestuous.en: The tempestuous sea frightened the sailors.
tempestuous.zh: 狂暴的大海吓坏了水手。

taciturn.en: The taciturn man rarely spoke at meetings.
taciturn.zh: 那个沉默寡言的人在会上很少说话。

taciturn.en: Her taciturn nature made her seem unfriendly.
taciturn.zh: 她沉默寡言的性格让她显得不友好。

stodgy.en: The stodgy pudding was hard to digest.
stodgy.zh: 那油腻的布丁很难消化。

stodgy.en: He disliked the stodgy food at the party.
stodgy.zh: 他不喜欢派对上油腻的食物。

reproof.en: She received a sharp reproof from her boss.
reproof.zh: 她受到了老板的严厉谴责。

reproof.en: His reproof made her feel ashamed.
reproof.zh: 他的责备让她感到羞愧。

accommodating.en: The accommodating host offered us a room.
accommodating.zh: 好客的主人给了我们一个房间。

accommodating.en: She was very accommodating to our needs.
accommodating.zh: 她非常通融地满足我们的需求。

aver.en: He averred that he was telling the truth.
aver.zh: 他坚称自己说的是实话。

aver.en: She averred her innocence in court.
aver.zh: 她在法庭上坚称自己无罪。

chirp.en: The birds chirp happily in the morning.
chirp.zh: 鸟儿在早晨快乐地吱喳叫。

chirp.en: I heard a chirp from the small bird.

adroit.en: She is adroit at solving complex problems.
His adroit handling of the situation impressed us.
adroit.zh: 他灵巧处理情况的方式让我们印象深刻。

warble.en: The bird began to warble a sweet song.
warble.zh: 鸟儿开始用颤音唱甜美的歌。

warble.en: She could warble like a nightingale.
warble.zh: 她能像夜莺一样颤声歌唱。

stultify.en: The boring lecture seemed to stultify the class.
stultify.zh: 无聊的讲座似乎让全班变得愚钝。

stultify.en: Repetitive tasks can stultify the mind.
stultify.zh: 重复的任务会使人思维迟钝。

sobriety.en: He maintained sobriety after quitting alcohol.
Sobriety is important for safe driving.
sobriety.zh: 清醒对安全驾驶很重要。

parlous.en: The parlous state of the economy worried everyone.
parlous.zh: 经济的危险状态让每个人担忧。

parlous.en: They faced a parlous journey through the mountains.
parlous.zh: 他们面临穿越山区的危险旅程。

meritorious.en: Her meritorious service earned her a medal.
meritorious.zh: 她有功绩的服务赢得了奖章。

meritorious.en: The meritorious student received a scholarship.
meritorious.zh: 那个值得称赞的学生获得了奖学金。

iniquitous.en: The iniquitous system oppressed the poor.
iniquitous.zh: 不公正的制度压迫穷人。

iniquitous.en: He condemned the iniquitous practices of the company.
iniquitous.zh: 他谴责公司邪恶的做法。

guzzle.en: He guzzled down the entire bottle of water.
The thirsty dog guzzled from the bowl.

funereal.en: The funereal atmosphere made everyone sad.
funereal.zh: 葬礼般的气氛让每个人都悲伤。

funereal.en: She wore a funereal black dress to the event.
funereal.zh: 她穿了一件葬礼般的黑色连衣裙参加活动。

espousal.en: Their espousal was celebrated with a feast.
espousal.zh: 他们的订婚用宴会庆祝。

espousal.en: The espousal of the cause united the group.
espousal.zh: 对这个事业的拥护团结了团体。

abstruse.en: The abstruse theory confused the students.
abstruse.zh: 深奥的理论让学生困惑。

abstruse.en: He wrote an abstruse article on philosophy.
abstruse.zh: 他写了一篇关于哲学的深奥文章。

tractable.en: The tractable horse obeyed every command.
tractable.zh: 驯服的马服从每个命令。

tractable.en: She found the child tractable and easy to teach.
tractable.zh: 她发现孩子听话且容易教。

tiff.en: They had a tiff over a small issue.
tiff.zh: 他们因小事发生了小争吵。

tiff.en: The tiff between friends was quickly resolved.
tiff.zh: 朋友间的小争吵很快解决了。

inviolable.en: The law considers human rights inviolable.
inviolable.zh: 法律认为人权不可侵犯。

inviolable.en: This sacred place is inviolable to all.
inviolable.zh: 这个神圣之地对所有人不可亵渎。

indoctrinate.en: The regime tried to indoctrinate the youth.
indoctrinate.zh: 政权试图灌输思想给年轻人。

indoctrinate.en: They indoctrinate new members with strict rules.
indoctrinate.zh: 他们用严格规则教导新成员。

gossamer.en: The morning dew hung on gossamer threads.
She wore a dress of fine gossamer.

emaciate.en: The illness caused him to emaciate quickly.
Without food, the animal began to emaciate.
emaciate.zh: 没有食物，动物开始消瘦。

bestial.zh: 他野兽般的行为震惊了所有人。

bestial.en: The crime was truly bestial in nature.

officious.en: The officious clerk annoyed the customers.
officious.zh: 多管闲事的职员惹恼了顾客。

officious.en: She gave officious advice to strangers.
officious.zh: 她向陌生人提供多管闲事的建议。

miscreant.en: The miscreant was caught by the police.
miscreant.zh: 那个恶棍被警察抓住了。

miscreant.en: No one trusted the known miscreant.
miscreant.zh: 没人信任那个臭名昭著的恶棍。

impudent.en: The impudent child talked back to his teacher.
impudent.zh: 那个鲁莽的孩子顶撞老师。

impudent.en: Her impudent remark made everyone uncomfortable.
impudent.zh: 她厚颜无耻的评论让所有人不舒服。

hoodwink.en: The con artist hoodwinked the old man.
They tried to hoodwink the investors.

impermeable.en: This jacket is impermeable to water.
The rock is impermeable to liquids.

demystify.en: The teacher helped demystify the math problem.
demystify.zh: 老师帮助解开了数学题的神秘面纱。

demystify.en: We need to demystify the process for beginners.
demystify.zh: 我们需要为初学者简化过程。

prefigure.en: The early signs prefigure a big change.
prefigure.zh: 早期迹象预示着一场大变化。
这个事件预示着未来的成功。

insincerity.en: I could sense his insincerity in the apology.
insincerity.zh: 我能感觉到他道歉中的不诚实。

insincerity.en: Her insincerity made the compliment feel fake.
insincerity.zh: 她的不诚实让赞美显得虚假。

whimsy.en: The story was full of whimsy and charm.
whimsy.zh: 故事充满了怪念头和魅力。

whimsy.en: She added a touch of whimsy to the room.
whimsy.zh: 她给房间增添了一丝离奇。

vacillate.en: He tends to vacillate between two choices.
vacillate.zh: 他倾向于在两个选择之间摇摆不定。

vacillate.en: Don't vacillate; make a decision now.
vacillate.zh: 别犹豫了，现在就做决定。

unbecoming.en: Such behavior is unbecoming of a leader.
unbecoming.zh: 这种行为不适合一个领导者。

unbecoming.en: Her dress was unbecoming for the formal event.
unbecoming.zh: 她的裙子不适合这个正式场合。

stickler.en: He is a stickler for punctuality.
My boss is a stickler about details.
stickler.zh: 我老板对细节一丝不苟。

prudish.en: She was too prudish to discuss the topic.
prudish.zh: 她过于拘谨，不愿讨论这个话题。

prudish.en: His prudish attitude surprised his friends.
prudish.zh: 他过分规矩的态度让朋友们惊讶。

inclement.en: The inclement weather forced us indoors.
inclement.zh: 恶劣的天气迫使我们待在室内。

inclement.en: They canceled the hike due to inclement conditions.
inclement.zh: 由于天气恶劣，他们取消了远足。

cornet.en: He played the cornet in the band.
The cornet has a bright, clear sound.
cornet.zh: 短号有明亮清晰的声音。

stoic.en: He remained stoic during the crisis.
A stoic person does not show much emotion.
stoic.zh: 淡泊的人不轻易表露情感。

spineless.en: The spineless manager never defended his team.
spineless.zh: 懦弱的经理从不维护他的团队。

spineless.en: She called him spineless for giving in so easily.
spineless.zh: 她骂他懦弱，因为他轻易屈服。

soporific.en: The lecture had a soporific effect on the students.
soporific.zh: 讲座对学生有催眠效果。

soporific.en: This warm milk is almost soporific.
soporific.zh: 这热牛奶几乎让人想睡。

sanctimonious.zh: 他假装虔诚的语气惹恼了所有人。

sanctimonious.en: She gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
sanctimonious.zh: 她发表了一篇关于诚实的伪善演讲。

rigmarole.en: We had to go through a lot of rigmarole.
rigmarole.zh: 我们不得不经历许多繁琐手续。

rigmarole.en: He told a long rigmarole about his trip.
rigmarole.zh: 他讲了一大堆关于旅行的废话。

raconteur.en: My grandfather was a wonderful raconteur.
raconteur.zh: 我祖父是个很棒的讲故事的人。

raconteur.en: The raconteur kept everyone entertained all night.
raconteur.zh: 那个健谈者让所有人整晚都很开心。

marionette.en: The children watched the marionette show.
marionette.zh: 孩子们看了牵线木偶表演。

marionette.en: He moved like a marionette on strings.
marionette.zh: 他像牵线木偶一样移动。

insularity.en: The island's insularity kept it unique.
insularity.zh: 岛屿的孤立使其保持独特。

insularity.en: Their insularity made them resistant to new ideas.
insularity.zh: 他们的孤立使他们抗拒新思想。

ignoble.en: His ignoble actions brought shame to the family.
ignoble.zh: 他卑鄙的行为给家族带来了耻辱。

exhume.en: The police decided to exhume the body.
They will exhume the remains for testing.
exhume.zh: 他们将发掘遗骸进行检测。

bedeck.en: They bedeck the hall with flowers.
The bride was bedecked in jewels.

vestigial.en: The human appendix is a vestigial organ.

venerate.en: They venerate the old temple as sacred.
venerate.zh: 他们崇敬这座古庙为圣地。

hieroglyphic.zh: 古埃及人使用象形文字。

hieroglyphic.en: The wall was covered in hieroglyphic symbols.
hieroglyphic.zh: 墙上布满了象形文字符号。

fetid.en: The fetid smell came from the swamp.
The room was filled with fetid air.
fetid.zh: 房间里充满了恶臭的空气。

depraved.en: The villain had a depraved mind.

depraved.zh: 这种道德败坏的行为不可接受。

amoral.zh: 年幼的孩子通常不分是非。

amoral.en: The amoral character cared only about profit.
amoral.zh: 那个不分是非的角色只关心利润。

starchy.zh: 土豆是一种淀粉类蔬菜。

starchy.en: He prefers starchy foods like bread and rice.
starchy.zh: 他更喜欢面包和米饭这类淀粉食物。

salutation.en: The letter began with a warm salutation.
He nodded as a salutation to his neighbor.

recumbent.en: She was recumbent on the sofa, resting.
The recumbent figure in the painting looked peaceful.
recumbent.zh: 画中躺着的形象看起来很平静。

fastness.en: The castle was a secure fastness.
fastness.zh: 城堡是一个坚固的要塞。

fastness.en: They retreated to their mountain fastness.
fastness.zh: 他们撤退到山中的要塞。

dilapidation.en: The old house was in a state of dilapidation.
Years of neglect led to the building's dilapidation.
dilapidation.zh: 多年的忽视导致建筑破损。

understated.en: Her dress was elegant and understated.
He preferred an understated style of decoration.
understated.zh: 他更喜欢朴素的装饰风格。

deportment.en: Her deportment at the party was excellent.
deportment.zh: 她在聚会上的举止非常得体。

deportment.en: Good deportment is important in formal settings.
deportment.zh: 良好的举止在正式场合很重要。

chauvinistic.en: His chauvinistic views offended many people.
chauvinistic.zh: 他的沙文主义观点冒犯了许多人。

chauvinistic.en: She criticized the chauvinistic attitude in the office.
chauvinistic.zh: 她批评了办公室里的性别歧视态度。

hedonist.en: He is a hedonist who loves luxury and pleasure.
hedonist.zh: 他是一个热爱奢华和享乐的享乐主义者。

hedonist.en: The hedonist spent all his money on vacations.
hedonist.zh: 那个享乐主义者把所有钱都花在度假上。

tendentious.en: The article was tendentious and unfair.
tendentious.zh: 那篇文章有偏见且不公平。

tendentious.en: His tendentious remarks caused a heated debate.
tendentious.zh: 他有倾向性的言论引发了激烈辩论。

stingy.en: He is too stingy to buy his friends gifts.
stingy.zh: 他太小气，不给朋友买礼物。

stingy.en: The stingy man never tips the waiter.
stingy.zh: 那个吝啬的人从不给服务员小费。

despoil.en: The invaders despoiled the village of its treasures.
despoil.zh: 入侵者掠夺了村庄的财宝。

despoil.en: They despoiled the forest for valuable timber.
despoil.zh: 他们为了珍贵木材掠夺了森林。

voluble.en: She is a voluble speaker who never stops talking.
voluble.zh: 她是个健谈的演讲者，从不停嘴。

voluble.en: His voluble explanation confused the audience.
voluble.zh: 他流利的解释让观众困惑。

tantalize.en: The smell of food tantalized the hungry children.
tantalize.zh: 食物的香味逗弄着饥饿的孩子们。

tantalize.en: She tantalized him with a promise she never kept.
tantalize.zh: 她用从未兑现的承诺逗弄他。

revelry.en: The streets were filled with revelry during the festival.
revelry.zh: 节日期间，街上充满了狂欢。

revelry.en: Their revelry kept the neighbors awake all night.
revelry.zh: 他们的狂欢让邻居整夜未眠。

repartee.en: Her quick repartee made everyone laugh.
repartee.zh: 她机智的妙语让大家都笑了。

repartee.en: He is known for his clever repartee in conversations.
repartee.zh: 他以对话中的巧妙反驳而闻名。

obeisance.en: The servant made a deep obeisance to the king.
They paid obeisance to the ancient tradition.
obeisance.zh: 他们对古老传统表示敬意。

feigned.en: She gave a feigned smile to hide her sadness.
feigned.zh: 她假装微笑以掩饰悲伤。

feigned.en: His feigned interest in the topic was obvious.
feigned.zh: 他对这个话题假装感兴趣是显而易见的。

botch.en: He botched the repair and made it worse.
botch.zh: 他拙劣地修补，反而弄得更糟。

botch.en: The chef botched the recipe and ruined the dish.
botch.zh: 厨师搞砸了食谱，毁了这道菜。

betoken.en: Dark clouds betoken a coming storm.
betoken.zh: 乌云预示着暴风雨即将来临。

betoken.en: His smile betokens a good mood today.
betoken.zh: 他的微笑预示着今天心情不错。

anticlimax.en: The movie's ending was a big anticlimax.
anticlimax.zh: 电影的结局是个大虎头蛇尾。

anticlimax.en: After the excitement, the quiet dinner felt like an anticlimax.
anticlimax.zh: 兴奋过后，安静的晚餐感觉像是个突降。

premeditated.en: The crime was clearly premeditated and planned.
premeditated.zh: 这起犯罪显然是预谋和计划好的。

premeditated.en: She made a premeditated decision to leave early.
premeditated.zh: 她做了预先考虑好的决定，提前离开。

overwrought.en: She was overwrought after the long argument.
overwrought.zh: 长时间争论后，她过度紧张。

overwrought.en: His overwrought emotions made him cry easily.
overwrought.zh: 他过度激动的情绪让他容易哭泣。

obdurate.en: He remained obdurate and refused to apologize.
The obdurate child would not listen to reason.
obdurate.zh: 那个执拗的孩子不听道理。

ingenuous.en: Her ingenuous smile showed her true feelings.
ingenuous.zh: 她天真的微笑显露了真实感受。

ingenuous.en: He was too ingenuous to hide his disappointment.
ingenuous.zh: 他太坦白了，无法掩饰失望。

hew.en: He used an axe to hew the wood.
They hew the stone to build a wall.

embitter.en: Failure can embitter a person over time.
embitter.zh: 失败会逐渐使一个人怨恨。

embitter.en: His harsh words embittered her for years.
embitter.zh: 他严厉的话语让她怨恨多年。

effeminate.en: Some people wrongly call him effeminate.
effeminate.zh: 有些人错误地称他女人气。

effeminate.en: His effeminate gestures were mocked by others.
effeminate.zh: 他柔弱的姿态被他人嘲笑。

contrition.en: He showed deep contrition for his mistake.
contrition.zh: 他对自己的错误表现出深深的悔悟。

contrition.en: Her contrition was evident in her tears.
contrition.zh: 她的悔改在眼泪中显而易见。

blithe.en: She had a blithe attitude about the risks.
blithe.zh: 她对风险抱着无忧无虑的态度。

blithe.en: His blithe disregard for rules annoyed everyone.
blithe.zh: 他轻率地无视规则，惹恼了大家。

untutored.en: He is untutored in the ways of business.
untutored.zh: 他对商业之道未受教育。

untutored.en: Her untutored talent amazed the music teacher.
untutored.zh: 她未经训练的天赋让音乐老师惊讶。

sentient.en: Humans are sentient beings with feelings.
sentient.zh: 人类是有感觉力的生物。

sentient.en: The robot was designed to be sentient.
sentient.zh: 这个机器人被设计成有知觉。

reportage.en: The reportage covered the event in detail.
reportage.zh: 新闻报道详细报道了该事件。
好的新闻报道需要准确的事实。

mortification.en: He felt great mortification after his public failure.
mortification.zh: 公开失败后，他感到极大的丢面子。

mortification.en: The monk practiced mortification through fasting.
mortification.zh: 僧侣通过禁食来实践禁欲。

interpolate.en: The editor tried to interpolate new data.
He interpolated a comment into the discussion.
interpolate.zh: 他在讨论中插入了一句评论。

insouciance.en: She faced the exam with insouciance.
insouciance.zh: 她无忧无虑地面对考试。

insouciance.en: His insouciance about the deadline worried us.
insouciance.zh: 他对截止日期的无忧无虑让我们担心。

gangling.en: The gangling teenager tripped over his own feet.
gangling.zh: 那个瘦长难看的少年被自己的脚绊倒了。

gangling.en: She was tall and gangling, like a giraffe.
gangling.zh: 她又高又瘦长，像只长颈鹿。

avarice.en: His avarice for money knew no bounds.
avarice.zh: 他对金钱的贪婪无止境。

avarice.en: Avarice drove him to cheat his friends.

unimpeachable.en: Her reputation is unimpeachable in the community.
unimpeachable.zh: 她在社区中的声誉无可指责。

unimpeachable.en: He provided unimpeachable evidence for his claim.
unimpeachable.zh: 他为自己的主张提供了无懈可击的证据。

autocrat.en: The autocrat ruled the country with an iron fist.
autocrat.zh: 独裁者用铁腕统治国家。

autocrat.en: People rebelled against the cruel autocrat.
autocrat.zh: 人民反抗残酷的独裁者。

colander.en: She used a colander to drain the pasta.
colander.zh: 她用滤器沥干意大利面。

colander.en: Wash the vegetables in a colander.

knoll.en: They climbed the grassy knoll to see the view.
A small knoll stood in the middle of the field.
knoll.zh: 田野中央有一个小圆丘。

bereave.en: The accident bereaved her of her husband.
War bereaves many families of their loved ones.
bereave.zh: 战争使许多家庭失去亲人。

wearisome.en: The long lecture was wearisome and boring.
wearisome.zh: 漫长的讲座令人疲倦且乏味。
他令人厌倦的抱怨惹恼了大家。

seclude.en: She decided to seclude herself in the mountains.
He wanted to seclude from the noisy city.

pilfer.en: He tried to pilfer a candy from the store.
pilfer.zh: 他试图从商店偷一颗糖。

pilfer.en: Someone pilfered my pen from the desk.
pilfer.zh: 有人从桌子上偷走了我的笔。

obsess.en: She tends to obsess over small details.
obsess.zh: 她容易在小细节上纠结。

obsess.en: Don't let fear obsess your mind.
obsess.zh: 别让恐惧占据你的思绪。

inveigh.en: He began to inveigh against the new policy.
The speaker inveighed loudly about corruption.

interstice.en: Light shone through an interstice in the wall.
interstice.zh: 光线从墙上的缝隙中透进来。

interstice.en: There is an interstice between the two rocks.
interstice.zh: 两块岩石之间有一个空隙。

enlightening.en: The lecture was very enlightening for everyone.
enlightening.zh: 这个讲座对大家很有启发。

enlightening.en: I found her book truly enlightening.
enlightening.zh: 我发现她的书确实发人深省。

astringent.en: The doctor used an astringent on the wound.
astringent.zh: 医生在伤口上用了收敛剂。

astringent.en: This fruit has an astringent taste.

vagrancy.en: Vagrancy is a problem in many big cities.
vagrancy.zh: 流浪在许多大城市是个问题。

vagrancy.en: He was arrested for vagrancy last night.

salve.en: She applied a salve to her sunburned skin.
salve.zh: 她在晒伤的皮肤上涂了药膏。

salve.en: His kind words were a salve for her heart.
salve.zh: 他体贴的话语安慰了她的心。

paean.en: The crowd sang a paean of victory.
paean.zh: 人群唱起了胜利的凯歌。

paean.en: They wrote a paean to honor the hero.
paean.zh: 他们写了一首赞美歌来纪念英雄。

nefarious.en: The villain had a nefarious plan.
nefarious.zh: 那个恶棍有一个恶毒的计划。

nefarious.en: Nefarious activities are punished by law.
nefarious.zh: 恶毒的活动会受到法律惩罚。

frisk.en: The puppies frisk around in the yard.
frisk.zh: 小狗们在院子里欢蹦乱跳。

frisk.en: The police officer stopped to frisk him.

equable.en: The climate here is equable all year.
equable.zh: 这里的气候全年都很稳定。

effete.en: The once powerful empire became effete.
effete.zh: 曾经强大的帝国变得衰微了。

effete.en: Effete aristocrats lost touch with reality.
effete.zh: 衰微的贵族脱离了现实。

dally.en: He likes to dally with new ideas.

curvaceous.en: The actress is known for being curvaceous.
curvaceous.zh: 这位女演员以曲线美著称。

tranquility.en: I love the tranquility of the forest.

slake.en: He tried to slake his curiosity.
slake.zh: 他试图满足自己的好奇心。

seafaring.en: He comes from a seafaring family.

magnanimity.en: He showed great magnanimity in defeat.
magnanimity.zh: 他在失败中表现出极大的宽宏大量。
她的宽宏大量打动了所有人。

iconoclastic.en: His iconoclastic views shocked many people.
iconoclastic.zh: 他打破旧习的观点震惊了许多人。

iconoclastic.en: She is known for her iconoclastic art.
iconoclastic.zh: 她以打破传统的艺术闻名。

eucalyptus.en: Eucalyptus oil has a strong smell.

dirge.en: They sang a dirge at the funeral.
dirge.zh: 他们在葬礼上唱了挽歌。

dirge.en: The music sounded like a dirge.

despotic.en: The despotic ruler oppressed the people.
despotic.zh: 专制的统治者压迫人民。

despotic.en: Despotic governments often ignore human rights.
despotic.zh: 专制政府常常忽视人权。

denouement.en: We finally reached the denouement of the drama.
denouement.zh: 我们终于看到了戏剧的结局。

combustible.en: Gasoline is a highly combustible liquid.
combustible.zh: 汽油是高度易燃的液体。

combustible.en: Keep combustible materials away from fire.

ennoble.en: Hard work can ennoble a person's character.
ennoble.zh: 努力工作能使人品格高尚。

ennoble.en: The king decided to ennoble the brave knight.
ennoble.zh: 国王决定授予勇敢的骑士爵位。

sweltering.en: It was a sweltering summer day.
The sweltering heat made everyone tired.
sweltering.zh: 闷热让每个人都疲惫不堪。

natty.en: He wore a natty suit to the party.
natty.zh: 他穿着整洁的西装去参加派对。

natty.en: She looked very natty in her new dress.
natty.zh: 她穿着新裙子看起来很帅气。

induct.en: They will induct the new president next week.
induct.zh: 他们下周将让新总统就职。

induct.en: The coach inducted him into the team.

geyser.en: The geyser erupted with hot water.
We saw a geyser in the national park.
geyser.zh: 我们在国家公园看到了一个间歇泉。

distend.en: The balloon began to distend with air.
distend.zh: 气球开始因充气而膨胀。

distend.en: His stomach distended after the big meal.

dalliance.en: He had a brief dalliance with his coworker.
dalliance.zh: 他和同事有过短暂的调情。

dalliance.en: Stop your dalliance and get to work.

corporeal.en: The ghost had no corporeal form.
We live in a corporeal world.
corporeal.zh: 我们生活在一个物质世界。

jamboree.en: The scouts held a big jamboree.
jamboree.zh: 童子军举办了一场大型聚会。

jamboree.en: We had a jamboree to celebrate the holiday.
jamboree.zh: 我们举办了一场欢乐聚会来庆祝节日。

cabal.en: A secret cabal plotted against the king.
cabal.zh: 一个秘密小集团密谋反对国王。

cabal.en: The cabal controlled the company from behind.
cabal.zh: 这个阴谋集团在幕后控制着公司。

cumulus.en: Cumulus clouds look like fluffy cotton.
cumulus.zh: 积云看起来像蓬松的棉花。

cumulus.en: A cumulus cloud floated across the sky.

catharsis.en: Crying can be a form of catharsis.
catharsis.zh: 哭泣可以是一种情感宣泄。

catharsis.en: The play provided an emotional catharsis.
catharsis.zh: 这部戏带来了情感上的净化。

burgeon.en: The city's population began to burgeon.
burgeon.zh: 这个城市的人口开始迅速增长。

burgeon.en: New businesses burgeon in the spring.
burgeon.zh: 新企业在春天蓬勃发展。

verbose.en: His verbose speech bored the audience.
verbose.zh: 他冗长的演讲让观众厌烦。

verbose.en: Try not to be too verbose in your writing.
verbose.zh: 写作时尽量不要过于冗长。

ticklish.en: He is very ticklish on his feet.
This is a ticklish situation to handle.
ticklish.zh: 这是一个难以处理的棘手局面。

seamy.en: The seamy side of the city is dangerous.
seamy.zh: 城市丑恶的一面很危险。

seamy.en: He saw the seamy reality of poverty.
seamy.zh: 他看到了贫困的丑恶现实。

lacerate.en: The broken glass lacerated his hand.
Her cruel words lacerated his heart.
lacerate.zh: 她残酷的话语使他的心很痛。

jarring.en: The jarring noise woke everyone up.
jarring.zh: 刺耳的噪音吵醒了所有人。

jarring.en: Their opinions were jarring and conflicting.
jarring.zh: 他们的意见不和谐且相互冲突。

fulminate.en: He fulminated against the new policy.
The chemical can fulminate if heated.
fulminate.zh: 这种化学物质加热会爆炸。

downplay.en: She tried to downplay her success.
downplay.zh: 她试图不予重视自己的成功。
不要不予重视所涉及的风险。

conviviality.en: The party was full of conviviality.
Their conviviality made everyone feel welcome.
conviviality.zh: 他们的欢乐让每个人都感到受欢迎。

thespian.en: She joined a local Thespian group.
thespian.zh: 她加入了一个当地的戏剧团体。

thespian.en: He is a talented Thespian actor.
thespian.zh: 他是一位有才华的戏剧演员。

loon.en: That loon is always causing trouble.
A loon swam quietly on the lake.
loon.zh: 一只潜鸟在湖上安静地游着。

kaleidoscopic.en: The sky had a kaleidoscopic range of colors.
kaleidoscopic.zh: 天空有千变万化的色彩。
她千变万化的想法让所有人惊讶。

gristle.en: I don't like eating gristle in meat.
gristle.zh: 我不喜欢吃肉里的软骨。

gristle.en: The steak had too much gristle.

frisky.en: The puppy was very frisky today.
Children are often frisky after a nap.
frisky.zh: 孩子们午睡后常常欢闹。

egregious.zh: 那是一个异乎寻常的错误。
他过分的举止震惊了所有人。

dishearten.en: The bad news disheartened the team.

disabuse.en: She disabused him of his false belief.
disabuse.zh: 她解除了他的错误信念。

disabuse.en: I need to disabuse you of that idea.
disabuse.zh: 我需要使你省悟那个想法。

coterminous.en: Their interests are coterminous with ours.
coterminous.zh: 他们的利益与我们的相连。

ventriloquist.en: She wants to become a ventriloquist.
ventriloquist.zh: 她想成为一名口技艺人。

titular.en: He is the titular head of the company.
titular.zh: 他是公司的名誉上的负责人。

titular.en: The titular role went to a famous actor.
titular.zh: 有头衔的角色给了一位著名演员。

spatula.en: Use a spatula to flip the pancake.
The doctor used a spatula to check her throat.
spatula.zh: 医生用压舌板检查她的喉咙。

obsequious.zh: 他谄媚的态度让我恼火。

obsequious.en: She gave an obsequious smile to the boss.
obsequious.zh: 她对老板露出了奉承的微笑。

measly.en: He only got a measly ten dollars.
measly.zh: 他只得到了微薄的十美元。

measly.en: That's a measly amount of food.
measly.zh: 那是少得可怜的食物量。

glutinous.en: The rice became glutinous after cooking.

envision.en: I envision a bright future for us.
envision.zh: 我预想我们有一个光明的未来。

envision.en: Can you envision living in space?

serried.en: The serried ranks of soldiers marched forward.
serried.zh: 密集的士兵队列向前行进。

serried.en: Serried trees lined the mountain path.
serried.zh: 林立的树木排列在山路上。

sacrilegious.zh: 那个行为被认为是冒渎的。

sacrilegious.en: He made a sacrilegious joke about the temple.
sacrilegious.zh: 他开了个关于寺庙的冒渎玩笑。

reedy.en: The reedy area was home to many birds.
reedy.zh: 芦苇丛生的区域是许多鸟的家。

reedy.en: He had a reedy voice that was hard to hear.
reedy.zh: 他有一个芦苇般细弱的声音，很难听到。

potentate.en: The potentate ruled with absolute power.
potentate.zh: 统治者以绝对权力统治。

potentate.en: A wealthy potentate lived in that palace.
potentate.zh: 一位有权势的统治者住在那座宫殿里。

mote.en: A mote of dust floated in the sunlight.
mote.zh: 一粒尘埃在阳光中漂浮。

mote.en: He saw a mote in her eye.
mote.zh: 他看到她眼里有一粒微粒。

malcontent.en: He is a malcontent who never smiles.
malcontent.zh: 他是一个从不微笑的不满者。

dilatory.en: His dilatory habits made us late.
dilatory.zh: 他拖拉的习惯让我们迟到了。

dilatory.en: She is too dilatory in her work.

crestfallen.en: He looked crestfallen after losing the game.
crestfallen.zh: 输掉比赛后他看起来垂头丧气。

crestfallen.en: She was crestfallen by the bad news.
crestfallen.zh: 她被坏消息弄得意气沮丧。

conciliate.en: He tried to conciliate the angry customer.
conciliate.zh: 他试图安抚愤怒的顾客。

conciliate.en: She conciliated both sides with a compromise.

unbend.en: He needs to unbend and relax a little.
She unbent the wire to make it straight.

incise.en: The surgeon incised the skin carefully.
incise.zh: 外科医生小心地切割皮肤。

incise.en: He incised his name on the stone.
incise.zh: 他把名字雕刻在石头上。

flange.en: The pipe has a flange for connection.
flange.zh: 管子有一个用于连接的凸缘。

flange.en: Tighten the bolts on the flange.

pliant.en: The pliant branch bent easily in the wind.
pliant.zh: 柔韧的树枝在风中容易弯曲。

pliant.en: She has a pliant personality and adapts well.
pliant.zh: 她性格柔顺，适应能力强。

epigram.en: He wrote a clever epigram for the contest.
epigram.zh: 他为比赛写了一个巧妙的警句。

epigram.en: Her speech ended with a witty epigram.
epigram.zh: 她的演讲以一个诙谐的警句结束。

upswing.en: The economy is on an upswing this year.
There was an upswing in sales last month.

neurology.en: She studies neurology at the university.
neurology.zh: 她在大学学习神经病学。
神经病学处理大脑疾病。

quaff.en: He quaffed the cold water quickly.
They quaffed beer at the party.
quaff.zh: 他们在派对上狂饮啤酒。

protuberance.en: A small protuberance appeared on the tree trunk.
protuberance.zh: 树干上出现了一个小突起。

protuberance.en: The doctor examined the protuberance on his skin.
protuberance.zh: 医生检查了他皮肤上的隆起物。

laggard.en: The laggard student finished the test last.
laggard.zh: 那个落后的学生最后一个完成测试。

laggard.en: Don't be a laggard in the race.
laggard.zh: 在比赛中不要做落后者。

hauteur.en: Her hauteur made her unpopular with colleagues.
hauteur.zh: 她的傲慢使她在同事中不受欢迎。

hauteur.en: He spoke with hauteur to the new employee.
hauteur.zh: 他以傲慢的态度对新员工说话。

equivocation.en: His equivocation made the audience confused.
equivocation.zh: 他的模棱两可让听众困惑。

equivocation.en: Politicians often use equivocation to avoid answers.
equivocation.zh: 政客们常用含糊话回避回答。

scalding.en: Be careful with the scalding hot water.
She received a scalding criticism from her boss.
scalding.zh: 她受到了老板尖锐辛辣的批评。

intermission.en: We bought snacks during the intermission.
intermission.zh: 我们在间歇期间买了零食。

intermission.en: The play had a short intermission after act one.
intermission.zh: 第一幕之后，戏剧有一个短暂的间歇。

hypodermic.en: The nurse used a hypodermic needle for the injection.
hypodermic.zh: 护士用皮下注射针头进行注射。

hypodermic.en: Hypodermic injections are common in hospitals.
hypodermic.zh: 皮下注射在医院很常见。

elongate.en: The artist tried to elongate the figure in the painting.
elongate.zh: 画家试图在画中拉长人物形象。

elongate.en: Stretching can help elongate your muscles.

dilettante.en: He is a dilettante who dabbles in many hobbies.
dilettante.zh: 他是一个浅尝辄止的业余爱好者。

dilettante.en: Her dilettante approach to art annoyed the experts.
dilettante.zh: 她对艺术的业余态度惹恼了专家。

debunk.en: Scientists debunked the myth about the moon.
debunk.zh: 科学家揭穿了关于月球的谬论。

debunk.en: The article aims to debunk common health myths.
debunk.zh: 这篇文章旨在揭穿常见的健康误区。

caprice.en: Her decision was a caprice, not a plan.
caprice.zh: 她的决定是一时任性，不是计划。

caprice.en: He bought the car on a sudden caprice.
caprice.zh: 他一时任性买了这辆车。

appetizing.en: The smell of the food was very appetizing.
She prepared an appetizing meal for dinner.
appetizing.zh: 她准备了一顿鲜美可口的晚餐。

stupefy.en: The loud noise seemed to stupefy the child.
stupefy.zh: 巨大的噪音似乎让孩子惊呆了。

stupefy.en: The drug can stupefy a patient for hours.
stupefy.zh: 这种药能使病人麻醉数小时。

remunerative.en: She found a remunerative job in the city.
remunerative.zh: 她在城里找到了一份有报酬的工作。

remunerative.en: Investing in stocks can be remunerative.
remunerative.zh: 投资股票可能有利可图。

pitiless.en: The pitiless storm destroyed many homes.
pitiless.zh: 无情的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。

pitiless.en: He gave a pitiless stare to the beggar.

offstage.en: The actors waited offstage for their cue.
offstage.zh: 演员们在幕后等待提示。

offstage.en: Her offstage life is very different from her role.
offstage.zh: 她的幕内生活与角色大不相同。

matador.en: The matador faced the bull with courage.
matador.zh: 斗牛士勇敢地面对公牛。

matador.en: A matador wears a special costume in the ring.
matador.zh: 斗牛士在斗牛场穿着特殊服装。

witticism.en: His witticism made everyone laugh at the party.
witticism.zh: 他的妙语让派对上每个人都笑了。

witticism.en: She is known for her clever witticism.
witticism.zh: 她以聪明的俏皮话闻名。

rakish.en: He wore a rakish hat tilted to one side.
rakish.zh: 他戴着一顶潇洒的帽子，歪向一边。

rakish.en: Her rakish smile charmed everyone in the room.
rakish.zh: 她潇洒的笑容迷住了房间里的每个人。

paroxysm.en: He had a paroxysm of coughing after running.
paroxysm.zh: 他跑步后一阵咳嗽发作。

paroxysm.en: The patient suffered a paroxysm of pain.
paroxysm.zh: 病人遭受了一阵疼痛的突发。

languor.en: A feeling of languor came over her in the heat.
languor.zh: 炎热中她感到一阵疲倦。

languor.en: The lazy afternoon filled him with languor.
languor.zh: 慵懒的下午让他充满怠惰。

finicky.en: My cat is finicky about its food.
He is finicky about the details of his work.
finicky.zh: 他对工作细节过分讲究。

brawny.en: The brawny man lifted the heavy box easily.
brawny.zh: 肌肉结实的男人轻松举起了重箱子。

brawny.en: She admired his brawny arms from working out.
brawny.zh: 她欣赏他锻炼出的强壮手臂。

bellicose.en: The bellicose nation threatened its neighbors.
bellicose.zh: 好战的国家威胁其邻国。

bellicose.en: His bellicose attitude started many fights.
bellicose.zh: 他的好斗态度引发了许多争斗。

aesthete.en: The aesthete appreciated every detail in the gallery.
aesthete.zh: 唯美主义者欣赏画廊里的每个细节。

aesthete.en: As an aesthete, she loves classical music.
aesthete.zh: 作为审美家，她热爱古典音乐。

actuate.en: The machine is actuated by a simple lever.
actuate.zh: 这台机器由一个简单的杠杆开动。

actuate.en: His speech actuated the crowd to take action.
actuate.zh: 他的演讲激励人群采取行动。

myopia.en: Myopia makes it hard to see distant objects.
myopia.zh: 近视使人难以看清远处的物体。

myopia.en: He wears glasses to correct his myopia.

miasma.en: A miasma of smoke hung over the city.
miasma.zh: 一股毒气般的烟雾笼罩着城市。

miasma.en: The swamp emitted a foul miasma.
miasma.zh: 沼泽散发出恶臭的瘴气。

oration.en: The president gave a moving oration at the ceremony.
oration.zh: 总统在典礼上发表了感人的演说。

oration.en: Her oration inspired the entire audience.
oration.zh: 她的致辞激励了全体观众。

interlace.en: The branches interlace to form a natural roof.
interlace.zh: 树枝交织形成天然屋顶。

interlace.en: She interlaces her fingers when she is nervous.

providential.en: It was providential that we found the lost key.
providential.zh: 我们找到丢失的钥匙真是幸运。

providential.en: The providential rain saved the crops.
providential.zh: 天佑的雨水拯救了庄稼。

rhapsody.en: He played a beautiful rhapsody on the piano.
rhapsody.zh: 他在钢琴上演奏了一首优美的狂想曲。

rhapsody.en: The poet recited a rhapsody about nature.
rhapsody.zh: 诗人朗诵了一首关于自然的狂文。

bilious.en: He felt bilious after eating too much rich food.
bilious.zh: 吃了太多油腻食物后，他感到胆汁不适。

bilious.en: Her bilious remarks upset everyone at the meeting.
bilious.zh: 她坏脾气的言论让会议上的每个人都不快。

instill.en: Teachers instill knowledge in their students.
Parents instill good values in their children.
instill.zh: 父母向孩子慢慢灌输良好的价值观。

verbiage.en: The report was full of unnecessary verbiage.
verbiage.zh: 报告充满了不必要的冗词。

verbiage.en: Avoid verbiage in your writing to be clear.
verbiage.zh: 写作中避免罗嗦以保持清晰。

sepulchral.en: The sepulchral silence in the cave was eerie.
sepulchral.zh: 洞穴中坟墓般的寂静令人毛骨悚然。

sepulchral.en: He spoke in a sepulchral voice that scared us.
sepulchral.zh: 他用阴沉的嗓音说话，吓到了我们。

peerless.en: Her peerless beauty amazed everyone at the event.
peerless.zh: 她无比的美貌惊艳了活动中的每个人。

peerless.en: The athlete's skill is peerless in the world.
peerless.zh: 这位运动员的技能在世界上无双。

gainsay.en: No one can gainsay the truth of his statement.
gainsay.zh: 没有人能否认他陈述的真实性。

gainsay.en: She dared to gainsay the popular opinion.
gainsay.zh: 她敢于反驳流行的观点。

apprise.en: Please apprise me of any changes in the plan.
apprise.zh: 请通知我计划中的任何变化。

apprise.en: He apprised his boss of the meeting's outcome.
apprise.zh: 他通知老板会议的结果。

superannuated.en: The superannuated teacher finally retired last year.
superannuated.zh: 那位年老退休的老师去年终于退休了。

superannuated.en: His superannuated ideas are no longer relevant.
superannuated.zh: 他过时的想法已不再相关。

sequester.en: The judge decided to sequester the jury.
They sequester the witness for safety.

quintessence.en: This painting is the quintessence of beauty.
Her speech captured the quintessence of the issue.
quintessence.zh: 她的演讲抓住了问题的精髓。

limber.en: She does stretches to keep her body limber.
limber.zh: 她做拉伸以保持身体柔软。

limber.en: The dancer is very limber and flexible.
limber.zh: 这位舞者非常柔软灵活。

levity.en: His levity during the meeting annoyed everyone.
levity.zh: 他在会议上的轻浮惹恼了所有人。

levity.en: We need seriousness, not levity, right now.
levity.zh: 我们现在需要严肃，而不是轻率。

commodious.en: The new house has a commodious living room.
commodious.zh: 新房子有一个宽敞的客厅。

commodious.en: This closet is commodious enough for all clothes.
commodious.zh: 这个壁橱足够宽敞，能放所有衣服。

carafe.en: Please bring a carafe of water to the table.
She poured wine from the glass carafe.

artless.en: Her artless smile made everyone feel welcome.
artless.zh: 她天真的微笑让每个人都感到受欢迎。

artless.en: The child's artless honesty was refreshing.
artless.zh: 孩子单纯的诚实令人耳目一新。

willowy.en: The model has a willowy figure.
She moved with a willowy grace.
willowy.zh: 她以优雅苗条的姿态移动。

wangle.en: He managed to wangle a free ticket.
wangle.zh: 他设法弄到了一张免费票。

wangle.en: She wangled her way into the exclusive party.
wangle.zh: 她耍手段进入了独家派对。

wallop.en: He gave the ball a powerful wallop.
The boxer walloped his opponent in the ring.
wallop.zh: 拳击手在台上猛击对手。

unprepossessing.en: The restaurant looks unprepossessing from outside.
unprepossessing.zh: 这家餐厅从外面看起来不吸引人。

unprepossessing.en: Despite his unprepossessing appearance, he is kind.
unprepossessing.zh: 尽管他外表不起眼，但他很善良。

rend.en: The loud noise rent the silence of the night.
rend.zh: 巨大的噪音划破了夜晚的寂静。

rend.en: The storm rent the old tree in two.
rend.zh: 暴风雨把老树劈成了两半。

querulous.en: The querulous child complained about everything.
querulous.zh: 那个爱发牢骚的孩子抱怨一切。

querulous.en: His querulous tone irritated his coworkers.
querulous.zh: 他抱怨的语气惹恼了同事。

pestle.en: She used a pestle to grind the spices.
The chemist ground the powder with a pestle.
pestle.zh: 化学家用杵把粉末磨碎。

peaky.en: He looked peaky after the long illness.
peaky.zh: 久病之后他看起来很消瘦。

peaky.en: The child's peaky face worried his mother.
peaky.zh: 孩子消瘦的脸让母亲担心。

nihilism.en: Nihilism rejects all moral and religious beliefs.
nihilism.zh: 虚无主义拒绝所有道德和宗教信仰。

nihilism.en: His philosophy of nihilism left him feeling empty.
nihilism.zh: 他的虚无主义哲学让他感到空虚。

muggy.en: The weather is muggy and uncomfortable today.
I hate the muggy summer afternoons.
muggy.zh: 我讨厌闷热的夏日午后。

inchoate.en: Her plan was still inchoate and unclear.
inchoate.zh: 她的计划仍然不成熟且不明确。

inchoate.en: The inchoate idea needed more development.
inchoate.zh: 这个初步的想法需要更多发展。

firebrand.en: He is a political firebrand who stirs up trouble.
firebrand.zh: 他是个煽动麻烦的政治煽动者。

firebrand.en: The firebrand threw a burning log into the crowd.
firebrand.zh: 煽动者把燃烧的木棍扔进人群。

dunce.en: The teacher called him a dunce for failing.
dunce.zh: 老师因他不及格而叫他傻瓜。

dunce.en: Don't be a dunce; study for the test.

avow.en: He avowed his love for her publicly.
avow.zh: 他公开承认了对她的爱。

avow.en: She avowed that she had made a mistake.
avow.zh: 她坦率承认自己犯了错误。

aorta.en: The aorta carries blood from the heart.
aorta.zh: 主动脉输送来自心脏的血液。

aorta.en: A blockage in the aorta is very dangerous.

adumbrate.en: The speaker adumbrated the main points of the talk.
adumbrate.zh: 演讲者概述了谈话的要点。

adumbrate.en: He adumbrated his plan in a few sentences.
adumbrate.zh: 他用几句话概括了他的计划。

riffle.en: He riffled through the pages of the book.
She riffled the deck of cards before dealing.

lank.en: Her hair was lank and lifeless after the rain.
lank.zh: 雨后她的头发又细又无生气。

lank.en: The lank grass lay flat on the ground.

ersatz.en: They drank ersatz coffee during the war.
ersatz.zh: 战争期间他们喝代用咖啡。

ersatz.en: The ersatz leather felt cheap and fake.
ersatz.zh: 代用皮革摸起来廉价又假。

drenched.en: He got drenched in the sudden rainstorm.
drenched.zh: 他在突如其来的暴雨中湿透了。

drenched.en: Her clothes were drenched with sweat after running.
drenched.zh: 跑步后她的衣服被汗水湿透。

byline.en: The article has a byline from a famous journalist.
byline.zh: 这篇文章有著名记者的署名。

byline.en: She earned a byline for her investigative report.
byline.zh: 她因调查报告获得了署名。

buffoon.en: The buffoon made everyone laugh at the party.
buffoon.zh: 小丑在派对上让所有人笑。

buffoon.en: Stop acting like a buffoon and be serious.

ragtime.en: Ragtime music was popular in the early 1900s.
ragtime.zh: 雷格泰姆音乐在20世纪初很流行。

ragtime.en: He played a lively ragtime tune on the piano.
ragtime.zh: 他在钢琴上弹奏了一首活泼的雷格泰姆曲调。

auger.en: He used an auger to drill a hole in the wood.
auger.zh: 他用螺旋钻在木头上钻孔。

auger.en: The auger made clean holes for the fence posts.
auger.zh: 螺旋钻为栅栏桩钻出了干净的洞。

proximate.en: The proximate cause of the accident was speed.
We need to find the proximate solution to the problem.
proximate.zh: 我们需要找到问题的最近解决方案。

magenta.en: She painted the room a bright magenta color.
magenta.zh: 她把房间漆成了亮品红色。

magenta.en: The flowers were a deep shade of magenta.

filch.en: He tried to filch a cookie from the jar.
filch.zh: 他试图从罐子里偷一块饼干。

filch.en: Someone filched my pen from the desk.
filch.zh: 有人从桌上偷了我的笔。

distracted.en: She was distracted by the noise outside.
distracted.zh: 她被外面的噪音弄得心烦意乱。

distracted.en: He felt distracted and couldn't focus on work.
distracted.zh: 他感到心烦意乱，无法专注于工作。

usury.en: The loan shark charged usury on the debt.
usury.zh: 高利贷者对债务收取高利。

usury.en: Usury is illegal in many countries.
usury.zh: 高利贷在许多国家是非法的。

isthmus.en: The Panama Canal connects the isthmus of Panama.
isthmus.zh: 巴拿马运河连接巴拿马地峡。

isthmus.en: They crossed the narrow isthmus to reach the island.
isthmus.zh: 他们穿过狭窄的地峡到达岛屿。

forger.en: The forger was arrested for making fake passports.
forger.zh: 伪造者因制作假护照被捕。

forger.en: He worked as a forger in the criminal ring.
forger.zh: 他在犯罪团伙中做伪造者。

hermetic.en: The container is hermetic to keep air out.
hermetic.zh: 容器是密封的以隔绝空气。

hermetic.en: The laboratory maintains a hermetic environment.

plebeian.en: He had plebeian tastes and simple habits.
plebeian.zh: 他有平民的品味和简单的习惯。

plebeian.en: The plebeian crowd cheered for the performer.
plebeian.zh: 平民人群为表演者欢呼。

alimentary.en: The alimentary canal helps digest food.
Good alimentary habits keep you healthy.
alimentary.zh: 良好的饮食习惯让你保持健康。

skittish.en: The skittish horse ran from the noise.
skittish.zh: 那匹易惊的马被噪音吓跑了。

skittish.en: She is skittish about trying new things.
skittish.zh: 她对尝试新事物感到紧张不安。

bombastic.en: His bombastic speech bored the audience.
bombastic.zh: 他夸夸其谈的演讲让观众厌烦。

bombastic.en: Avoid bombastic language in simple writing.
bombastic.zh: 在简单的写作中避免夸大的语言。

unexceptionable.en: Her behavior was unexceptionable at the party.
unexceptionable.zh: 她在聚会上的行为无可挑剔。

unexceptionable.en: The plan seemed unexceptionable to everyone.
unexceptionable.zh: 这个计划对每个人来说都无懈可击。

serendipity.en: Finding that book was pure serendipity.
serendipity.zh: 找到那本书纯属意外之喜。

serendipity.en: Serendipity led her to a new career.
serendipity.zh: 机缘巧合让她找到了新职业。

odium.en: The politician faced public odium for lying.
odium.zh: 那位政客因撒谎而招致公众憎恶。

odium.en: His actions brought odium upon the family.
odium.zh: 他的行为给家族带来了耻辱。

nauseate.en: The smell of rotten eggs nauseates me.
nauseate.zh: 臭鸡蛋的气味让我恶心。

nauseate.en: Violence in movies can nauseate some people.
nauseate.zh: 电影中的暴力会让一些人感到厌恶。

leaven.en: Add leaven to the dough to make it rise.
leaven.zh: 在面团中加入酵母使其发酵。

leaven.en: Humor can leaven a serious conversation.
leaven.zh: 幽默可以缓和严肃的谈话。

imponderable.en: The outcome depends on many imponderable factors.
imponderable.zh: 结果取决于许多无法估量的因素。

imponderable.en: Luck is an imponderable in any success.
imponderable.zh: 运气是任何成功中无法衡量的因素。

ennui.en: He felt a deep ennui during the long meeting.
ennui.zh: 在漫长的会议中他感到深深的倦怠。

ennui.en: Ennui set in after weeks of doing nothing.
ennui.zh: 几周无所事事之后，厌倦感袭来。

drivel.en: Stop talking drivel and be serious.
His speech was nothing but drivel.
drivel.zh: 他的演讲全是胡言乱语。

circumlocution.en: He used circumlocution to avoid answering directly.
circumlocution.zh: 他使用迂回的说法来避免直接回答。

circumlocution.en: Circumlocution can make a simple point confusing.
circumlocution.zh: 迂回的说法会让简单的观点变得令人困惑。

bamboozle.en: The scammer tried to bamboozle the old man.
bamboozle.zh: 骗子试图欺骗那位老人。

bamboozle.en: Don't let his charm bamboozle you.
bamboozle.zh: 别让他的魅力迷惑了你。

ablution.en: The priest performed the ritual ablution before prayer.
ablution.zh: 牧师在祈祷前进行了仪式性的沐浴。

ablution.en: Ablution is part of many religious traditions.
ablution.zh: 沐浴是许多宗教传统的一部分。

tardy.en: She was tardy for the morning class again.
A tardy response can cause problems.
tardy.zh: 迟到的回复可能会引发问题。

lassitude.en: A feeling of lassitude came over him after work.
lassitude.zh: 下班后他感到一阵倦怠。

lassitude.en: Lassitude made it hard to get out of bed.

inveigle.en: He inveigled her into joining the club.
inveigle.zh: 他诱骗她加入了俱乐部。

inveigle.en: They tried to inveigle him with promises of money.
inveigle.zh: 他们试图用金钱的承诺诱骗他。

effrontery.en: He had the effrontery to ask for a raise.
effrontery.zh: 他厚颜无耻地要求加薪。

effrontery.en: Her effrontery shocked everyone in the room.
effrontery.zh: 她的厚颜无耻震惊了房间里的每个人。

credulous.en: Credulous people often fall for scams.
credulous.zh: 轻信的人常常上当受骗。

credulous.en: She is too credulous to question his story.
credulous.zh: 她太轻信了，不会质疑他的说法。

certitude.en: He spoke with certitude about the future.
Certitude can sometimes lead to stubbornness.

abrade.en: The rough surface will abrade your skin.
abrade.zh: 粗糙的表面会擦伤你的皮肤。

abrade.en: Wind and sand abrade the ancient stones.
abrade.zh: 风和沙磨损了古老的石头。

spendthrift.en: A spendthrift quickly wastes all his money.
spendthrift.zh: 挥霍无度的人很快就会花光所有的钱。

spendthrift.en: She is a spendthrift who loves shopping.
spendthrift.zh: 她是个挥霍无度的人，喜欢购物。

simpleton.en: Don't be a simpleton and believe everything.
simpleton.zh: 别像个傻子一样什么都信。

simpleton.en: He was called a simpleton for his naive ideas.
simpleton.zh: 他因为天真的想法而被叫做笨蛋。

rumple.en: The wind rumpled her hair as she walked.
rumple.zh: 她走路时风吹乱了她的头发。

rumple.en: Don't rumple the clean sheets on the bed.
rumple.zh: 别把床上的干净床单弄皱。

rollicking.en: The children had a rollicking time at the park.
rollicking.zh: 孩子们在公园里玩得欢闹。

rollicking.en: It was a rollicking party full of laughter.
rollicking.zh: 那是一个充满笑声的欢乐派对。

protean.en: His protean talents include acting and writing.
protean.zh: 他多变的才华包括表演和写作。

protean.en: The protean nature of the cloud makes it fascinating.
protean.zh: 云朵千变万化的特性令人着迷。

obsolescent.en: This technology is obsolescent and rarely used.
obsolescent.zh: 这项技术正在被淘汰，很少使用了。

obsolescent.en: Obsolescent machines are replaced by new ones.
obsolescent.zh: 过时的机器被新机器取代。

irredeemable.en: The debt was considered irredeemable by the bank.
irredeemable.zh: 银行认为这笔债务无法偿还。

irredeemable.en: His reputation is irredeemable after the scandal.
irredeemable.zh: 丑闻之后他的名誉无法挽回。

impostor.en: The impostor pretended to be a doctor.
impostor.zh: 那个冒名顶替者假装成医生。

impostor.en: They caught the impostor before he could steal anything.
impostor.zh: 他们在他偷东西之前抓住了那个骗子。

exactitude.en: The scientist values exactitude in measurements.
exactitude.zh: 科学家重视测量的精确性。

exactitude.en: Exactitude is important in legal documents.
exactitude.zh: 精确性在法律文件中很重要。

doff.en: He doffed his hat as a sign of respect.
Please doff your coat when entering the house.

amity.en: The two countries signed a treaty of amity.
Amity between neighbors makes life pleasant.
amity.zh: 邻里之间的友好让生活愉快。

agape.en: The children stood agape at the magic show.
agape.zh: 孩子们在魔术表演前目瞪口呆。

agape.en: He stared agape at the unexpected news.
agape.zh: 他目瞪口呆地盯着这个意外的消息。

roughen.en: Cold weather can roughen your skin.
roughen.zh: 寒冷的天气会使你的皮肤变粗糙。

roughen.en: The sandpaper will roughen the wood surface.
roughen.zh: 砂纸会使木头表面变粗糙。

occlude.en: A blood clot can occlude an artery.
The clouds occlude the sun completely.

incorruptible.en: The judge was known to be incorruptible.
An incorruptible leader earns the people's trust.
incorruptible.zh: 一个清廉的领导者赢得人民的信任。

detestable.zh: 撒谎是一种可憎的习惯。

detestable.en: His detestable behavior made everyone angry.
detestable.zh: 他可憎的行为让每个人都生气。

debility.en: Old age often brings physical debility.
debility.zh: 老年常常带来身体虚弱。

debility.en: The illness left him in a state of debility.
debility.zh: 疾病使他处于虚弱状态。

agog.en: The children were agog with excitement.
She was agog to hear the latest news.
agog.zh: 她急切地想听到最新消息。

repugnance.en: She felt repugnance at the sight of blood.
His repugnance for violence is well known.
repugnance.zh: 他对暴力的厌恶是众所周知的。

jamb.en: He leaned against the door jamb.

condescend.en: She would not condescend to speak to us.
condescend.zh: 她不肯屈尊和我们说话。
不要对你的同学摆架子。

unbidden.en: Tears came unbidden to her eyes.
unbidden.zh: 泪水不由自主地涌上她的眼眶。

unbidden.en: He arrived unbidden at the party.
unbidden.zh: 他未经邀请就来到了派对。

sterilize.en: Doctors sterilize surgical tools before use.
sterilize.zh: 医生在使用前消毒手术工具。

sterilize.en: You should sterilize the baby's bottle.
sterilize.zh: 你应该给婴儿的奶瓶消毒。

reaper.en: The reaper worked hard in the field.
reaper.zh: 收割者在田里辛勤劳作。

reaper.en: A modern reaper can harvest quickly.
reaper.zh: 现代收割机能快速收割。

preempt.en: The news will preempt regular programming.
She tried to preempt their criticism.
preempt.zh: 她试图先发制人地阻止他们的批评。

aerate.en: You should aerate the soil for plants.
aerate.zh: 你应该给土壤通气以利植物生长。

aerate.en: The machine helps aerate the wine.
aerate.zh: 这台机器帮助给葡萄酒充气。

procrastinate.en: Do not procrastinate on your homework.
He tends to procrastinate when stressed.

dispensable.en: This old chair is dispensable now.
dispensable.zh: 这把旧椅子现在可有可无。

dispensable.en: Some items in the kit are dispensable.
dispensable.zh: 工具箱里有些物品不是必需的。

ejaculate.en: He ejaculated a sudden cry of surprise.
The doctor studied how men ejaculate.
ejaculate.zh: 医生研究男性如何射精。

trapeze.en: The acrobat swung on the trapeze.
trapeze.zh: 杂技演员在秋千上荡来荡去。

trapeze.en: She learned to fly on a trapeze.
trapeze.zh: 她学会了在吊秋千上飞翔。

unctuous.en: His unctuous manner made me uneasy.
unctuous.zh: 他虚情假意的态度让我不安。

unctuous.en: She gave an unctuous smile to the boss.
unctuous.zh: 她对老板露出谄媚的微笑。

purloin.en: Someone purloined my wallet on the bus.
purloin.zh: 有人在公交车上偷了我的钱包。

purloin.en: He purloined a cookie from the jar.
purloin.zh: 他从罐子里偷了一块饼干。

opinionated.en: He is very opinionated about politics.
opinionated.zh: 他对政治非常固执己见。
固执己见的人很少听别人意见。

loquacious.en: The loquacious man talked for hours.
loquacious.zh: 那个多嘴的男人聊了好几个小时。

loquacious.en: She is loquacious at every meeting.
loquacious.zh: 她在每次会议上都很健谈。

estimable.en: She is an estimable teacher in our school.
estimable.zh: 她是我们学校一位可敬的老师。

estimable.en: His estimable work earned him respect.
estimable.zh: 他可敬的工作赢得了尊重。

elephantine.zh: 那个巨大的生物缓慢移动。

elephantine.en: His elephantine footsteps shook the floor.
elephantine.zh: 他笨重的脚步震动了地板。

efface.en: Time will efface the painful memories.
efface.zh: 时间会抹去痛苦的记忆。

efface.en: She tried to efface herself from the group.
efface.zh: 她试图在群体中不引人注目。

clairvoyant.zh: 那个有洞察力的人预测了未来。

clairvoyant.en: She has a clairvoyant ability to see truths.

atone.en: He tried to atone for his mistake.
atone.zh: 他试图弥补自己的错误。

atone.en: She atoned by helping the community.
atone.zh: 她通过帮助社区来赎罪。

vandalize.zh: 有人破坏了公园的长椅。

portend.en: Dark clouds portend a coming storm.
portend.zh: 乌云预示着暴风雨即将来临。

portend.en: This event may portend future trouble.
portend.zh: 这个事件可能预示着未来的麻烦。

hidebound.zh: 他顽固的观点阻碍了进步。

hidebound.en: She is too hidebound to try new things.
hidebound.zh: 她太死板，不愿尝试新事物。

gyrate.en: The dancer began to gyrate on stage.
gyrate.zh: 舞者在舞台上开始旋转。
直升机的旋翼快速旋转。

expeditious.en: We need an expeditious solution to this.
expeditious.zh: 我们需要一个迅速的解决方案。

expeditious.en: The expeditious delivery pleased the customer.
expeditious.zh: 迅速的送货让顾客满意。

evanescent.en: The beauty of a sunset is evanescent.

evanescent.zh: 她转瞬即逝的微笑很快消失了。

cataclysm.en: The earthquake was a terrible cataclysm.
cataclysm.zh: 地震是一场可怕的灾难。

cataclysm.en: War can cause a social cataclysm.
cataclysm.zh: 战争可能导致社会大变动。

abjure.en: He abjured his former beliefs publicly.
abjure.zh: 他公开宣布放弃以前的信仰。

abjure.en: She abjured violence in her speech.
abjure.zh: 她在演讲中发誓放弃暴力。

sublimate.zh: 艺术可以升华强烈的情感。

sublimate.en: He sublimated his anger into creative work.
sublimate.zh: 他把愤怒升华为创造性工作。

sinecure.en: His job is a sinecure with little work.
sinecure.zh: 他的工作是个闲职，几乎没活干。

sinecure.en: She found a sinecure at the office.
sinecure.zh: 她在办公室找了个闲差。

sensitize.en: The campaign aims to sensitize the public.
sensitize.zh: 这项运动旨在提高公众的敏感度。

sensitize.en: We need to sensitize people to this issue.
sensitize.zh: 我们需要让人们对此问题敏感起来。

propitiate.en: They offered gifts to propitiate the gods.
propitiate.zh: 他们献上礼物以安抚神灵。

propitiate.en: He tried to propitiate his angry boss.
propitiate.zh: 他试图安抚生气的老板。

offbeat.en: She has an offbeat sense of humor.
offbeat.zh: 她有一种不落俗套的幽默感。

offbeat.en: The movie has an offbeat storyline.
offbeat.zh: 这部电影的情节很离奇。

necropolis.en: The ancient necropolis was discovered here.
necropolis.zh: 古代大墓地在这里被发现。
游客参观了古老的坟场。

jabber.en: The children jabbered excitedly in the room.
jabber.zh: 孩子们在房间里兴奋地叽叽喳喳。

jabber.en: I could not understand his jabber.
jabber.zh: 我听不懂他含糊不清的话。

hippopotamus.en: The hippopotamus lives in the river.
A hippopotamus can be very dangerous.

friable.en: The dry soil is friable and crumbly.
friable.zh: 干燥的土壤易碎且松散。
易碎的岩石很容易碎裂。

elocution.en: She took lessons to improve her elocution.
elocution.zh: 她上课来提高自己的演讲技巧。

elocution.en: His elocution was clear and powerful.

cadge.en: He always tries to cadge a free meal.
cadge.zh: 他总是试图讨一顿免费饭。

cadge.en: She cadged a ride from her friend.

slipshod.en: His slipshod work disappointed the teacher.
slipshod.zh: 他马虎的工作让老师失望。

slipshod.en: A slipshod attitude leads to mistakes.
slipshod.zh: 马虎的态度会导致错误。

pedant.en: The pedant corrected every small grammar mistake.
pedant.zh: 那个书呆子纠正了每一个小的语法错误。

pedant.en: Don't be such a pedant about the rules.

overreach.en: He tried to overreach and lost everything.
overreach.zh: 他试图做得过头，结果失去了一切。

overreach.en: The company overreached by expanding too fast.
overreach.zh: 公司扩张过快，做得过火了。

byproduct.en: Honey is a byproduct of flower pollination.
byproduct.zh: 蜂蜜是花朵授粉的副产品。

byproduct.en: Stress can be a byproduct of hard work.
byproduct.zh: 压力可能是努力工作的副产品。

febrile.en: The child felt febrile and stayed in bed.
A febrile patient needs plenty of water.
febrile.zh: 发热的病人需要多喝水。

debrief.en: The pilot will debrief after the mission.
debrief.zh: 飞行员将在任务后汇报情况。

debrief.en: We need to debrief the team about the project.
debrief.zh: 我们需要向团队听取项目报告。

apostasy.en: His apostasy shocked the entire community.
apostasy.zh: 他的叛教震惊了整个社区。

apostasy.en: Apostasy is rare in that strict religion.
apostasy.zh: 在那个严格的宗教中，背教很少见。

transfigure.en: The sunset transfigured the sky with colors.
transfigure.zh: 日落用色彩改变了天空。

transfigure.en: Love can transfigure a person's life completely.
transfigure.zh: 爱能彻底改变一个人的生活。

monocle.en: He wore a monocle to read the small print.
monocle.zh: 他戴着单片眼镜看小字。

monocle.en: The old gentleman adjusted his monocle carefully.
monocle.zh: 那位老先生小心地调整了他的单片眼镜。

substratum.en: The soil has a rocky substratum underneath.
substratum.zh: 土壤下面有一个岩石基层。

substratum.en: Trust is the substratum of any friendship.
substratum.zh: 信任是任何友谊的基础。

parka.en: She wore a warm parka in the snow.
parka.zh: 她在雪地里穿了一件温暖的派克大衣。

parka.en: His parka has a hood for the rain.
parka.zh: 他的派克大衣有防雨的帽子。

megalomania.en: His megalomania made him think he was a king.
megalomania.zh: 他的夸大狂让他以为自己是个国王。

megalomania.en: Megalomania can lead to unrealistic ambitions.
megalomania.zh: 夸大狂会导致不切实际的野心。

interregnum.en: The country had an interregnum after the king died.
interregnum.zh: 国王死后，国家有一段空位期。

interregnum.en: During the interregnum, no one was in charge.

fop.en: That fop spends hours on his appearance.
fop.zh: 那个花花公子花几个小时打扮自己。

fop.en: He is a fop who only cares about fashion.
fop.zh: 他是个只关心时尚的花花公子。

erasure.en: The erasure of the mistake took time.
She noticed an erasure on the paper.
erasure.zh: 她注意到纸上有一处擦除的痕迹。

ostracism.en: Ostracism from the group hurt her deeply.
ostracism.zh: 被团体排斥深深伤害了她。

ostracism.en: He faced ostracism for his unpopular opinions.
ostracism.zh: 他因不受欢迎的观点而遭到排斥。

unenlightened.en: The unenlightened villagers feared new ideas.
unenlightened.zh: 愚昧无知的村民害怕新思想。

unenlightened.en: An unenlightened person may reject science.
unenlightened.zh: 未受启发的人可能会拒绝科学。

transience.en: The transience of youth makes it precious.
He accepted the transience of all things.

torpid.en: The bear was torpid during winter hibernation.
torpid.zh: 熊在冬眠期间是迟钝的。

torpid.en: He felt torpid after the long illness.
torpid.zh: 久病之后他感到迟缓无力。

stipple.en: The artist used stipple to create texture.
stipple.zh: 艺术家用点刻法创造纹理。

stipple.en: She learned to stipple with a fine brush.
stipple.zh: 她学会了用细刷子点画。

scrumptious.en: The cake was absolutely scrumptious and rich.
She made a scrumptious dinner for everyone.
scrumptious.zh: 她为大家做了一顿可口的晚餐。

premeditate.en: He did not premeditate the crime at all.
premeditate.zh: 他完全没有预谋这起犯罪。

premeditate.en: They premeditate every step of the plan.
premeditate.zh: 他们预先考虑了计划的每一步。

ebullience.en: Her ebullience filled the room with joy.
ebullience.zh: 她的热情洋溢让房间充满欢乐。

ebullience.en: The child's ebullience was contagious to all.
ebullience.zh: 孩子的热情洋溢感染了所有人。

unflappable.en: She remained unflappable during the crisis.
An unflappable pilot can handle emergencies well.
unflappable.zh: 镇定的飞行员能很好地处理紧急情况。

obtrude.en: He tends to obtrude his opinions on others.
obtrude.zh: 他倾向于把自己的意见强加给别人。

obtrude.en: Don't obtrude into their private conversation.
obtrude.zh: 不要强行闯入他们的私人谈话。

modish.en: She wore a modish dress to the party.
modish.zh: 她穿了一条时髦的裙子去派对。

modish.en: His modish haircut attracted many compliments.
modish.zh: 他时髦的发型吸引了许多赞美。

iconoclast.en: The artist was an iconoclast who broke traditions.
iconoclast.zh: 这位艺术家是个打破传统的反对偶像崇拜者。

iconoclast.en: An iconoclast often challenges popular beliefs.
iconoclast.zh: 提倡打破旧习的人常常挑战流行信仰。

fumigate.en: They fumigate the house to kill pests.
fumigate.zh: 他们熏制房子以杀死害虫。

fumigate.en: The doctor will fumigate the hospital room.

expostulate.en: She tried to expostulate with him about his plan.
expostulate.zh: 她试图劝诫他关于他的计划。

expostulate.en: He would expostulate against risky decisions.
expostulate.zh: 他会告诫反对冒险的决定。

enfeeble.en: The disease can enfeeble even strong people.
enfeeble.zh: 疾病甚至能使强壮的人衰弱。

enfeeble.en: Age will enfeeble the body over time.
enfeeble.zh: 年龄会逐渐使身体衰弱。

dissolute.en: He led a dissolute life full of parties.
dissolute.zh: 他过着放荡的生活，充满派对。

dissolute.en: The dissolute man spent all his money on fun.
dissolute.zh: 那个放荡的人把所有钱都花在享乐上。

acme.en: She reached the acme of her career at forty.
acme.zh: 她在四十岁达到了事业的顶点。

acme.en: The acme of his success was winning the award.
acme.zh: 他成功的顶点是赢得奖项。

umbrage.en: He took umbrage at her critical comments.
umbrage.zh: 他对她的批评感到不快。

umbrage.en: She felt umbrage when they ignored her idea.
